title: Antiseizure medication dosing
scopeNotes: Adults; maintenance and titration only — loading doses live in the status epilepticus entries and load calculators
CRRT dosing not covered — no institutional or published source supplied; ask pharmacy
Phenobarbital: no current FDA-approved adult label; card sourced from the AES 2024 ASM summary

entries.title: Levetiracetam (Keppra) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Partial-onset (adults ≥16 y): start 500 mg q12h; may ↑ by 1000 mg/day every 2 weeks; max 3000 mg/day. JME myoclonic and PGTC: same start, titrate to 3000 mg/day
notes: Label: no evidence that >3000 mg/day adds benefit

renal.label: ESRD on dialysis
renal.doseText: 500–1000 mg q24h, plus a 250–500 mg supplemental dose after dialysis
notes: ~50% of body levetiracetam removed by a standard 4-h hemodialysis (label §12.3)

renalNotes: Label bands use CrCl normalized to BSA: CrCl (mL/min) from Cockcroft-Gault × 1.73 / BSA (m²) (§2.7)
No pediatric renal dosing in label
hepatic: No adjustment: mild–moderate PK unchanged; severe (Child-Pugh C) clearance ↓50%, mostly from reduced renal clearance (§12.3)
ivPo: IV ↔ PO 1:1: same total daily dose and frequency in both directions (§2.4–2.5)
IV: dilute in 100 mL NS, LR or D5W; give over 15 min (§2.6)
No clinical study experience with IV levetiracetam beyond 4 days (§2.1)
enteral: Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
interactions: Unlikely to cause or be subject to PK interactions; not CYP450-dependent (§12.3)
pearls: Avoid abrupt withdrawal — risk of increased seizures and status epilepticus (§2.8)
Elderly: renally cleared — dose by renal function (§8.5)
sources: Keppra (levetiracetam) injection US prescribing information. UCB; revised 6/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Lacosamide (Vimpat) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Adults ≥17 y: start 100 mg BID; ↑ by 50 mg BID weekly; maintenance 150–200 mg BID (300–400 mg/day)
Adults ≥17 y: start 50 mg BID; ↑ by 50 mg BID weekly; maintenance 100–200 mg BID (200–400 mg/day)
notes: Adjunctive trials: >400 mg/day was not more effective and had substantially more adverse reactions

maintenance.agent: Lacosamide — alternate initial regimen (faster to maintenance)
maintenance.doseText: Adults ≥17 y: single 200 mg loading dose, then 100 mg BID starting 12 h later for 1 week; then titrate weekly if needed
notes: Give the load under medical supervision — more CNS and cardiovascular adverse reactions (§2.2)

renal.label: CrCl <30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault) or ESRD
renal.doseText: Reduce the maximum dosage by 25% (300 mg/day if the maximum is 400 mg/day)

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: Effectively removed by HD; after a 4-h session consider supplementing up to 50% of the dose

renalNotes: In all renal impairment, start and titrate by response and tolerability (§2.4)
With strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors, a dose reduction may be needed in renal impairment (§2.4)
hepatic: Mild or moderate: reduce the maximum dosage by 25% (§2.5)
Severe: not recommended (§2.5)
With strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors, a dose reduction may be needed in hepatic impairment (§2.5)
ivPo: IV and oral dosing are the same (§2.1)
IV over 30–60 min; adults may receive it over as little as 15 min if required (§2.7)
IV experience limited to 5 consecutive days (§2.1)
enteral: Tablets: swallow whole; do not divide (§2.6)
Oral solution may be given via NG or gastrostomy tube (§2.6)
interactions: Strong CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitors: dose reduction may be needed with renal or hepatic impairment (§2.4–2.5)
Phenytoin/fosphenytoin may lower lacosamide levels (Cerebyx label Table 7)
pearls: IV can cause bradycardia, AV block and ventricular tachyarrhythmia; ECG before starting and at steady state if proarrhythmic conditions or conduction-affecting drugs (§2.7)
Withdraw gradually over ≥1 week (§2.8)
sources: Vimpat (lacosamide) tablets, injection, oral solution US prescribing information. UCB; revised 5/2026 (user-supplied label)
Cerebyx (fosphenytoin sodium) injection US prescribing information. Pfizer; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Brivaracetam (Briviact) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Adults ≥16 y: 50 mg BID; adjust to 25–100 mg BID (50–200 mg/day) by response and tolerability; no titration needed

renalNotes: No adjustment for renal impairment (§8.6)
<10% excreted unchanged; HD not expected to enhance clearance (§10)
hepatic: All Child-Pugh classes: start 25 mg BID; max 75 mg BID (150 mg/day) (§2.5, Table 2)
ivPo: IV = PO: same dose and frequency; tablets, solution and injection interchangeable (§2.1, §12.3)
IV over 2–15 min; undiluted or in NS, LR or D5W (§2.3)
IV experience up to 4 consecutive days (§2.1)
enteral: Tablets: swallow whole; do not chew or crush (§2.2)
Oral solution may be given via NG or gastrostomy tube (§2.2)
interactions: Rifampin: increase brivaracetam dose by up to 100% (§2.6, §7.1)
Phenytoin: brivaracetam can raise phenytoin levels — monitor levels when adding or stopping (§7.3)
Carbamazepine: ↑ carbamazepine-epoxide; reduce carbamazepine if not tolerated (§7.2)
CYP2C19 poor metabolizers or CYP2C19 inhibitors may need a lower dose (§12.3)
pearls: No added benefit when combined with levetiracetam (§7.4)
Psychiatric adverse reactions (irritability, psychosis) can occur (§5.3)
sources: Briviact (brivaracetam) tablets, oral solution, injection US prescribing information. UCB; revised 4/2026 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Valproate (Depacon IV / Depakote) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Adults and children ≥10 y: start 10–15 mg/kg/day; ↑ by 5–10 mg/kg/day weekly to response; max 60 mg/kg/day. Divide if >250 mg/day
notes: Label maximum 60 mg/kg/day (not expressible as a DoseCap — per-kg)
Elderly: lower starting dose, slower titration (§2.2)
evidenceNote: Valproate sodium injection label §2.1–2.2; Depakote label §2.2

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: No dose adjustment per label; HD lowers valproate concentrations ~20%

renalNotes: No adjustment in renal failure; CrCl <10 mL/min: unbound clearance ↓27% (IV label §12.3)
Protein binding substantially reduced in renal failure — total levels may mislead (IV label §12.3)
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction (label §4)
Hepatic disease: free levels may be high while total looks normal (IV label §12.3)
ivPo: Oral → IV: same total daily dose, same frequency; infuse over 60 min, ≤20 mg/min (IV label §2.1)
IV–oral equivalence shown only with q6h dosing; with BID/TID IV dosing, troughs may be lower — monitor trough levels (IV label §2.1)
IV use >14 days not studied — switch to oral when feasible (IV label §2.1)
Valproic acid → Depakote: same daily dose and schedule; once stable, BID or TID may be used (Depakote §2.2)
enteral: Depakote delayed-release: swallow whole; do not crush or chew (Depakote §2.1)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: Usual therapeutic range 50–100 mcg/mL total (epilepsy)
Thrombocytopenia risk rises at total ≥110 mcg/mL (women) or ≥135 mcg/mL (men)

Free fraction rises with concentration (~10% at 40 → 18.5% at 130 mcg/mL) and is higher in elderly, hyperlipidemia, hepatic and renal disease — total level is not a reliable index of active drug (IV label §12.2–12.3)
interactions: Carbapenems (meropenem, imipenem, ertapenem): clinically significant ↓ valproate levels with loss of seizure control — monitor levels; change antibiotic or ASM if levels drop
Phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital can double valproate clearance (IV label §7.1)
Aspirin: valproate free fraction ↑ ~4-fold (IV label §7.1)
Lamotrigine: valproate more than doubles lamotrigine levels — lamotrigine dose must be reduced; ↑ serious rash risk
Phenytoin: valproate displaces phenytoin (free fraction +60% in volunteers) — use free phenytoin levels; combination ↑ hyperammonemia risk
Topiramate: hyperammonemia and encephalopathy (IV label §7.3)
pearls: Check ammonia for unexplained lethargy, vomiting or mental-status change (label §5)
Boxed warnings: hepatotoxicity, fetal risk, pancreatitis
Contraindicated with POLG mitochondrial disease and urea cycle disorders (label §4)
sources: Valproate sodium injection US prescribing information. Hikma; revised 12/2023 (user-supplied label)
Depakote (divalproex sodium) delayed-release tablets US prescribing information. AbbVie; revised 3/2026 (user-supplied label)
Lamictal (lamotrigine) tablets, tablets for oral suspension, ODT US prescribing information. GlaxoSmithKline; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)
Cerebyx (fosphenytoin sodium) injection US prescribing information. Pfizer; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Phenytoin / fosphenytoin — maintenance dosing and levels

maintenance.doseText: Adult initial maintenance 4–6 mg PE/kg/day in divided doses; ≤150 mg PE/min; then individualize by levels
notes: Continuous ECG, BP and respiratory monitoring during and after IV infusion (boxed warning)
IM ordinarily not used (§2.4)

maintenance.doseText: Adults: start 100 mg TID; most need 100 mg TID–QID; max 200 mg TID. Once-daily 300 mg only with extended capsules, once controlled on 100 mg TID
Adults: start 125 mg (5 mL) TID; up to 625 mg (25 mL)/day
notes: Free acid — ~8% more phenytoin than the sodium-salt products (capsules, IV); monitor levels when switching (§2.4)

renalNotes: No renal dose table; unbound fraction ↑ in renal disease — dose and monitor by free levels (Cerebyx §2.7; Dilantin §2.5)
After IV fosphenytoin in renal/hepatic disease or hypoalbuminemia, conversion to phenytoin may outpace phenytoin clearance → more adverse events (Cerebyx §2.7)
Fosphenytoin phosphate load 0.0037 mmol/mg PE — consider in severe renal impairment (Cerebyx §5.12)
Labels give no hemodialysis dosing
hepatic: Liver impairment: early toxicity possible; monitor unbound levels (Cerebyx §8.6)
ivPo: Oral phenytoin → fosphenytoin IV/IM: same total daily mg PE; levels may rise modestly (capsules ~90% bioavailable vs 100% IV/IM) (Cerebyx §2.6)
1 mg PE = 1 mg phenytoin sodium — no conversion between fosphenytoin and phenytoin sodium (Cerebyx §2.1, §5.1)
Suspension (free acid) ↔ capsules/IV (sodium salt): ~8% difference in drug content — monitor levels (Dilantin §2.4)
enteral: Enteral feeds lower phenytoin levels — don't give with a feed; check levels more often (Dilantin §7.4)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: Target 10–20 mcg/mL total; 1–2 mcg/mL free (Cerebyx §2.5; Dilantin §2.3)
Use free levels in renal or hepatic disease, hypoalbuminemia and pregnancy (Cerebyx §2.7, §2.9)
After fosphenytoin, wait ~2 h after IV (4 h after IM) to draw — immunoassays overestimate before conversion; if earlier, use EDTA tube (Cerebyx §2.5)
Steady state takes 7–10 days; don't change dose more often than every 7–10 days (Dilantin §2.3, §12.3)
Saturable metabolism: a ≥10% dose increase can raise levels disproportionately (Dilantin §12.3)
Toxicity is variable: nystagmus ~20, ataxia ~30, dysarthria/lethargy >40 mcg/mL (Cerebyx §10)
interactions: Valproate: displaces phenytoin and inhibits its metabolism — use free levels; ↑ hyperammonemia risk (Cerebyx §7.3)
Brivaracetam can raise phenytoin levels (Briviact §7.3)
Phenytoin lowers levels of apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, ticagrelor, nimodipine, lamotrigine (~40%) and lacosamide (Cerebyx Table 7; Lamictal Table 13)
TMP-SMX: ↑ phenytoin toxicity risk
Warfarin: PT/INR can rise or fall (Cerebyx Table 7)
pearls: IV contraindicated with sinus bradycardia, SA block, 2nd/3rd-degree AV block, Adams-Stokes (Cerebyx §4)
CYP2C9 *2/*3 carriers: start low and follow levels (Cerebyx §8.7)
Correction equations are estimates — see calc:phenytoin-correction; a measured free level is preferred
sources: Cerebyx (fosphenytoin sodium) injection US prescribing information. Pfizer; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)
Dilantin (extended phenytoin sodium capsules) US prescribing information. Viatris; revised 8/2023 (DailyMed setid 86dd27d1-9cee-48ae-b55d-e2d2f7dbc593, accessed 2026-11-06)
Phenytoin oral suspension 125 mg/5 mL US prescribing information. Sun Pharmaceutical; revised 8/2025 (user-supplied label)
Briviact (brivaracetam) tablets, oral solution, injection US prescribing information. UCB; revised 4/2026 (user-supplied label)
Lamictal (lamotrigine) tablets, tablets for oral suspension, ODT US prescribing information. GlaxoSmithKline; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)

Kiang TK, Ensom MH. A comprehensive review on the predictive performance of the Sheiner-Tozer and derivative equations for the correction of phenytoin concentrations. Ann Pharmacother 2016;50(4):311-325. doi:10.1177/1060028016628166

entries.title: Lamotrigine (Lamictal) — titration

maintenance.doseText: Wk 1–2: 25 mg every other day. Wk 3–4: 25 mg daily. Then ↑ 25–50 mg/day every 1–2 wk. Usual maintenance 100–200 mg/day (valproate alone) or 100–400 mg/day (valproate + inducers), in 1–2 doses
Wk 1–2: 25 mg daily. Wk 3–4: 50 mg daily. Then ↑ 50 mg/day every 1–2 wk. Usual maintenance 225–375 mg/day in 2 doses

maintenance.agent: Lamotrigine — WITH carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital or primidone (no valproate)
maintenance.doseText: Wk 1–2: 50 mg/day. Wk 3–4: 100 mg/day in 2 doses. Then ↑ 100 mg/day every 1–2 wk. Usual maintenance 300–500 mg/day in 2 doses
notes: Rifampin and lopinavir/ritonavir: use this column (§2.2)

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: No supplemental dose stated; ~20% of body lamotrigine removed per 4-h session (§12.3)

renalNotes: Start per concomitant medications; reduced maintenance doses may be effective in significant renal impairment; little experience in severe impairment — use caution (§2.1, §8.7)
Half-life roughly doubles in chronic renal failure (§8.7)
hepatic: Mild: no adjustment (§2.1)
Moderate or severe without ascites: reduce initial, escalation and maintenance doses by ~25% (§2.1)
Severe with ascites: reduce by ~50% (§2.1)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation in label (§3)
enteral: Tablets for oral suspension: swallow whole, chew, or disperse in a small amount of water or diluted juice and take all of it (§2.5)
ODT: place on tongue; with or without water (§2.6)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: No established therapeutic range — dose by response; levels may help with interacting drugs (§2.1, §5.14)
interactions: Valproate: lamotrigine levels ↑ slightly more than 2-fold (Table 13)
Carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital/primidone, rifampin: lamotrigine ↓ ~40% (Table 13)
Estrogen-containing OCs: lamotrigine ↓ ~50%; maintenance often needs up to 2×; levels rise in the pill-free week (§2.1, §5.9)
Lopinavir/ritonavir ↓ ~50%; atazanavir/ritonavir ↓ ~32% (Table 13)
Avoid OCT2 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index (e.g., dofetilide) (§7)
pearls: Serious rash risk ↑ with valproate, exceeding the initial dose or escalation, HLA-B*1502; most within 2–8 weeks; stop at first rash unless clearly not drug-related (boxed warning)
Off >5 half-lives: restart with the initial titration; don't restart after lamotrigine rash unless benefit clearly outweighs risk (§2.1)
Class IB antiarrhythmic activity in vitro — weigh risk in structural/functional heart disease (§5.4)
Can cause false-positive PCP on rapid urine drug screens (§5.14)
Taper over ≥2 weeks (~50%/week) unless safety requires faster (§2.1)
sources: Lamictal (lamotrigine) tablets, tablets for oral suspension, ODT US prescribing information. GlaxoSmithKline; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Oxcarbazepine (Trileptal / Oxtellar XR) — maintenance dosing and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Adults: start 600 mg/day BID; ↑ by ≤600 mg/day at ~weekly intervals. Adjunctive: recommended 1200 mg/day. Conversion to monotherapy: up to 2400 mg/day
notes: Adjunctive >1200 mg/day: somewhat more effective, but most patients couldn't tolerate 2400 mg/day (CNS effects) (§2.1)
Strong CYP3A4 or UGT inducers: dose adjustment recommended (§2.1, §7.2)

maintenance.doseText: Adults: 600 mg once daily for 1 week; ↑ by 600 mg/day weekly to 1200–2400 mg once daily. With strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin) or UGT inducers (rifampin): consider starting 900 mg once daily
notes: Take on an empty stomach (≥1 h before or ≥2 h after meals) — food raises peak levels and adverse reactions (§2.1)
Geriatric: consider starting 300 or 450 mg/day; ↑ by 300–450 mg/day weekly (§2.4)

renal.label: CrCl <30 mL/min
renal.doseText: Start at half the usual starting dose (300 mg/day; IR given BID) and increase slowly. XR: ↑ by 300–450 mg/day weekly

renalNotes: CrCl <30 mL/min: MHD half-life prolonged to 19 h, AUC 2-fold (Trileptal §12.3)
Label units are mL/min, not BSA-normalized
Labels give no hemodialysis dosing
hepatic: Mild–moderate: no effect on oxcarbazepine or MHD PK (Trileptal §12.3)
Severe: not evaluated; Oxtellar XR not recommended (Oxtellar §8.7)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation (Trileptal §3; Oxtellar §3)
enteral: Trileptal oral suspension 300 mg/5 mL (60 mg/mL); tablets and suspension substitute at equal doses (Trileptal §2.8, §3)
Suspension: shake well; may be mixed in a small glass of water or given straight from the syringe (Trileptal §2.8)
Oxtellar XR: swallow whole — do not cut, crush or chew; for difficulty swallowing use multiples of lower-strength tablets (Oxtellar §2.1)
XR once daily is not bioequivalent to IR BID: at 1200 mg/day, XR MHD AUC and Cmax ~19% lower, Cmin ~16% lower (Oxtellar §12.3). IR → XR may need higher doses (§2.7); no label XR → IR conversion
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: MHD 10–35 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
With strong CYP3A4/UGT inducers, monitor MHD levels during titration (Trileptal §7.2)
interactions: Phenytoin: levels rise with oxcarbazepine >1200 mg/day — monitor phenytoin levels; phenytoin dose may need to be reduced (Trileptal §7.1)
Strong CYP450/UGT inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) ↓ MHD 25–49%; adjust when inducers are started, changed or stopped (Trileptal §7.2)
Perampanel: oxcarbazepine ↓ perampanel levels (Fycompa §7.2)
pearls: Hyponatremia: Na <125 mmol/L in 2.5% in trials; usually in the first 3 months, sometimes after >1 year; SIADH reported. Check Na with other Na-lowering drugs or symptoms (nausea, lethargy, confusion, more seizures) (Trileptal §5.1)
Elderly: MHD AUC 30–60% higher (age-related CrCl); close Na monitoring if at risk (Trileptal §8.5)
~25–30% of patients with carbamazepine hypersensitivity react to oxcarbazepine (Trileptal §5.3)
Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to oxcarbazepine or eslicarbazepine (Trileptal §4)
Withdraw gradually; rapid stop can be considered for a serious adverse event (Trileptal §5.6)
sources: Trileptal (oxcarbazepine) film-coated tablets and oral suspension US prescribing information. Novartis; revised 10/2026 (user-supplied label)
Oxtellar XR (oxcarbazepine) extended-release tablets US prescribing information. Supernus Pharmaceuticals; revised 10/2026 (user-supplied label)
Fycompa (perampanel) tablets and oral suspension US prescribing information. Catalyst Pharmaceuticals; revised 1/2024 (user-supplied label)

Vossler DG, Gidal BE; American Epilepsy Society Treatments Committee. A Summary of Antiseizure Medications Available in the United States, 4th edition. American Epilepsy Society; revised April 1, 2024 (user-supplied)

entries.title: Carbamazepine (Tegretol / Tegretol-XR) — maintenance dosing and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Adults and children >12 y: start 200 mg BID (tablets or XR) or 100 mg (1 tsp) QID (suspension) = 400 mg/day; ↑ by up to 200 mg/day weekly — XR BID, other forms TID–QID. Usual maintenance 800–1200 mg/day. Generally ≤1200 mg/day above age 15; up to 1600 mg/day in adults in rare instances

dose.label: Maintenance
frequency: XR: BID; tablets or suspension: TID–QID

notes: Take with meals (D&A)
When added to other ASMs, add gradually; phenytoin may have to be increased (D&A)
evidenceNote: Tegretol label, Dosage and Administration (epilepsy, >12 y) and Dosage Information table

renalNotes: No renal dose adjustment in label
hepatic: Baseline and periodic LFTs, especially with a history of liver disease; stop for new or worsening liver dysfunction or active liver disease (Precautions, Laboratory Tests)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation in label (Description)
enteral: Suspension 100 mg/5 mL. Tablets → suspension: same mg/day in smaller, more frequent doses (BID tablets → TID suspension) (D&A)
Suspension gives higher peaks than tablets at the same dose — start low (D&A; Clinical Pharmacology)
Don't give the suspension at the same time as other liquid medicines or diluents — precipitate with chlorpromazine and thioridazine solutions (D&A; Precautions)
XR: swallow whole, never crush or chew; discard damaged tablets or those without a release portal. Tablets → XR: same total daily dose (D&A)
Suspension contains propylene glycol 25 mg/mL — count total propylene glycol from all sources (Description; Warnings)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: Usual adult therapeutic level 4–12 mcg/mL (Clinical Pharmacology)
Autoinduction completes after 3–5 weeks; half-life 25–65 h initially, 12–17 h on repeated dosing (Clinical Pharmacology)
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors ↑ carbamazepine: macrolides, azoles, isoniazid, diltiazem, verapamil, cimetidine, omeprazole, fluoxetine, protease inhibitors, grapefruit juice — monitor levels (Precautions, Drug Interactions)
Valproate, brivaracetam, quetiapine, loxapine ↑ carbamazepine-epoxide — adjust dose or monitor (Precautions)
Inducers ↓ carbamazepine: phenytoin/fosphenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, rifampin, felbamate, theophylline, cisplatin, doxorubicin (Precautions)
Avoid with apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran and edoxaban — anticoagulant levels may be inadequate (Precautions)

Lowers levels of many drugs, incl. warfarin, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, corticosteroids (dexamethasone, prednisolone), lamotrigine, valproate, phenytoin, topiramate, zonisamide, oxcarbazepine, methadone, haloperidol, clozapine, aripiprazole (double its dose) (Precautions)
Resistance to nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers (pancuronium, vecuronium, rocuronium, cisatracurium) — faster recovery, higher infusion rates (Precautions)
Lithium: ↑ neurotoxicity risk (Precautions)
Nefazodone: contraindicated. MAOIs: stop ≥14 days before (Contraindications)
Cenobamate ↓ carbamazepine (Xcopri Table 5); perampanel ↓ by carbamazepine (Fycompa §7.2)
pearls: Hyponatremia, often SIADH; risk dose-related, higher in elderly and with diuretics; consider stopping if symptomatic (Warnings, General)
Boxed warnings: SJS/TEN with HLA-B*1502; aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis
Avoid in hepatic porphyria (Warnings, General)
Withdraw gradually (Warnings, General)
IV carbamazepine (Carnexiv) is not in this label — confirm availability with pharmacy
sources: Tegretol (carbamazepine) tablets and suspension; Tegretol-XR extended-release tablets US prescribing information. Novartis; revised 8/2026 (user-supplied label)
Xcopri (cenobamate) tablets US prescribing information. SK Life Science; revised 8/2025 (user-supplied label)
Fycompa (perampanel) tablets and oral suspension US prescribing information. Catalyst Pharmaceuticals; revised 1/2024 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Topiramate (Topamax) — maintenance dosing and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Start 25–50 mg/day; ↑ by 25–50 mg/day weekly. Recommended 200–400 mg/day in 2 divided doses (focal or LGS); 400 mg/day for PGTC. >400 mg/day no added benefit (focal)
notes: 25 mg/day weekly increments may delay reaching an effective dose (§2.2)

maintenance.doseText: Target 400 mg/day in 2 doses: 25 mg BID wk 1, 50 BID wk 2, 75 BID wk 3, 100 BID wk 4, 150 BID wk 5, 200 BID wk 6

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: A supplemental dose may be required; label gives no amount — base it on dialysis duration, dialyzer clearance and the patient's renal clearance
notes: HD clears topiramate 4–6 times faster than normal (§8.7); 120 mL/min dialyzer clearance vs 20–30 mL/min total oral clearance (§12.3)

renalNotes: Moderate (30–69) and severe (<30 mL/min/1.73 m²) impairment both reduce clearance (§8.6)
Elderly: adjust for age-related CrCl <70 mL/min/1.73 m² (§8.5)
hepatic: Moderate–severe: plasma clearance ↓ ~26%; no dose rule in label (§12.3)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation (§3)
enteral: Tablets: don't break — bitter taste (§2.4)
Sprinkle capsules 15 mg and 25 mg: swallow whole, or open and sprinkle the entire contents on a teaspoon of soft food; swallow immediately without chewing; don't store (§2.4, §3)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: 7–30 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
interactions: Phenytoin ↓ topiramate 48%; carbamazepine ↓ 40% — dose adjustment may be needed (§7.1, Table 11)
Valproate: hyperammonemia with or without encephalopathy, and hypothermia — check ammonia (§5.14, §5.16, §7.1)
Other carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (zonisamide, acetazolamide): more severe acidosis, kidney stones — monitor (§7.2)
Lithium: exposure ↑ at high-dose topiramate — monitor levels (§7.7)
Hydrochlorothiazide ↑ topiramate; dose decrease may be needed (§7.5)
pearls: Hyperchloremic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis at any time; baseline and periodic bicarbonate. Additive with renal disease, severe respiratory disorders, status epilepticus, diarrhea, ketogenic diet (§5.4)
Acute myopia and secondary angle-closure glaucoma: stop as soon as possible (§5.1)
Encephalopathic symptoms: measure ammonia (§5.14)
Withdraw gradually (§5.8)
sources: Topamax (topiramate) tablets and sprinkle capsules US prescribing information. Janssen Pharmaceuticals; revised 3/2026 (user-supplied label)

Vossler DG, Gidal BE; American Epilepsy Society Treatments Committee. A Summary of Antiseizure Medications Available in the United States, 4th edition. American Epilepsy Society; revised April 1, 2024 (user-supplied)

entries.title: Clobazam (Onfi / Sympazan) — maintenance dosing and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Label dosing (LGS, ≥2 y): ≤30 kg: 5 mg/day → 10 mg/day from day 7 → 20 mg/day from day 14. >30 kg: 10 → 20 → 40 mg/day. >5 mg/day in 2 divided doses; escalate no faster than weekly
notes: Label indication is adjunctive treatment of LGS only (§1)
Steady state: clobazam 5 days, N-desmethylclobazam 9 days (§2.1)

renalNotes: No adjustment for mild or moderate renal impairment; essentially no experience in severe impairment or ESRD; dialyzability unknown (Onfi §2.6, §8.7)
hepatic: Mild–moderate (Child-Pugh 5–9): start 5 mg/day; titrate to half the Table 1 doses; may titrate to the maximum from day 21 (Onfi §2.7)
Severe: no dosing recommendation (Onfi §2.7)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation (Onfi §3; Sympazan §3)
enteral: Onfi tablets 10 and 20 mg: whole, broken in half along the score, or crushed and mixed in applesauce (Onfi §2.3)
Onfi oral suspension 2.5 mg/mL; shake well; use the supplied syringe and adapter (Onfi §2.3, §3)
Sympazan oral film 5, 10, 20 mg: on top of the tongue; don't give with liquids; one film at a time; bioequivalent to clobazam tablets (Sympazan §2.3, §12.3)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: Clobazam 30–300 ng/mL; N-desmethylclobazam 300–3000 ng/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
interactions: Opioids: profound sedation, respiratory depression, death — limit dose and duration (boxed warning; Onfi §7.1)
Strong (fluconazole, fluvoxamine, ticlopidine) or moderate (omeprazole) CYP2C19 inhibitors: up to 5-fold ↑ N-desmethylclobazam — dose adjustment may be needed (Onfi §7.4, §12.3)
Cenobamate ↑ N-desmethylclobazam — consider a lower clobazam dose (Xcopri Table 5)
Phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine: no significant change in clobazam or N-desmethylclobazam PK (Onfi §12.3)
CYP2D6 substrates: lower doses may be needed (Onfi §7.3)
Alcohol ↑ clobazam exposure ~50% (Onfi §7.2)
pearls: Boxed warnings: opioids; abuse, misuse and addiction; dependence and withdrawal
Taper: ↓ total daily dose by 5–10 mg/day weekly; abrupt stop can cause life-threatening withdrawal (Onfi §2.2)
Elderly or known CYP2C19 poor metabolizers: start 5 mg/day; titrate to half the Table 1 doses (Onfi §2.4–2.5)
Half-life 36–42 h; N-desmethylclobazam 71–82 h (Onfi §12.3)

entries.title: Zonisamide (Zonegran / Zonisade) — maintenance dosing and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Adults >16 y: 100 mg daily; after 2 weeks 200 mg/day; then 300 and 400 mg/day, each stable ≥2 weeks. 100–600 mg/day effective; no suggestion of more response above 400 mg/day; max 600 mg/day. Once or twice daily
notes: Steady state up to 2 weeks after each change (half-life ~63 h) (Zonegran D&A, Clinical Pharmacology)
evidenceNote: Zonegran label, Dosage and Administration; Zonisade label §2.2

renalNotes: Avoid in renal failure (estimated GFR <50 mL/min) — insufficient dosing and toxicity experience (Zonegran Precautions; Zonisade §8.6)
Stop with acute renal failure or a sustained clinically significant ↑ creatinine/BUN (Zonegran Precautions; Zonisade §8.6)
Mean ~8% ↑ creatinine and BUN, interpreted as a GFR effect (Zonegran Precautions)
Renal disease: caution, slower titration, more frequent monitoring (Zonegran D&A)
hepatic: Not studied; caution, slower titration, more frequent monitoring (Zonegran D&A, Clinical Pharmacology)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation (Zonegran How Supplied; Zonisade §3)
enteral: Zonegran capsules 25 and 100 mg: swallow whole (Zonegran D&A)
Zonisade oral suspension 100 mg/5 mL; same mg dosing as capsules; shake well; use an accurate measuring device; discard 30 days after opening (Zonisade §2.2–2.3, §3)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: 10–40 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
interactions: Phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital shorten zonisamide half-life to 27–38 h (vs ~63 h); dose adjustment may be needed when inducers are started, changed or stopped; monitor with rifampin (Zonegran Clinical Pharmacology)
CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, cimetidine): no dose change needed (Zonegran Clinical Pharmacology)
Other carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (topiramate, acetazolamide): more severe acidosis, hyperammonemia, kidney stones — monitor (Zonegran Clinical Pharmacology; Zonisade §7.2)
pearls: Sulfonamide: contraindicated with sulfonamide or zonisamide hypersensitivity (Zonegran Contraindications)
Hyperchloremic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis: baseline and periodic bicarbonate (Zonegran Warnings; Zonisade §2.1)
Taper gradually (Zonisade §2.4)
sources: Zonegran (zonisamide) capsules US prescribing information. Advanz Pharma; revised 9/2026 (user-supplied label)
Zonisade (zonisamide) oral suspension US prescribing information. Azurity Pharmaceuticals; revised 9/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Cenobamate (Xcopri) — titration and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Adults: 12.5 mg once daily wk 1–2; 25 mg wk 3–4; 50 mg wk 5–6; 100 mg wk 7–8; 150 mg wk 9–10; 200 mg once daily from wk 11. If needed ↑ by 50 mg every 2 weeks to max 400 mg once daily. Don't exceed this schedule
notes: Faster titration risks serious adverse reactions incl. DRESS (§2.2, §5.1)

renalNotes: Mild–moderate (CLcr 30 to <90 mL/min) and severe (<30 mL/min): use with caution; dose reduction may be considered (§8.6)
hepatic: Baseline ALT, AST and total bilirubin before starting if none within 3 months (§2.1)
Mild–moderate (Child-Pugh A–B): max 200 mg once daily; further reduction may be considered (§2.3, §8.7)
Severe (Child-Pugh C): not recommended (§2.3)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation (§3)
enteral: Tablets may be crushed, mixed with 25 mL water and given by mouth or NG tube; flush with 10 mL water; confirm no particles remain (§2.4)
Crushed tablets by mouth or NG tube: Cmax and AUC similar to whole tablets; median Tmax 0.5 h (§12.3)
levels: 10–35 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
interactions: Phenytoin: up to 2-fold ↑ — gradually ↓ phenytoin dose by up to 50% during titration (§7.1, Table 5)
Phenobarbital and N-desmethylclobazam ↑ — consider reducing phenobarbital or clobazam (Table 5)
Lamotrigine and carbamazepine ↓ — increase as needed (Table 5)
CYP2C19 substrates ↑ (consider reducing); CYP2B6 and CYP3A substrates ↓ (increase as needed) (Table 5)
Drugs that shorten QT: use caution (§7.2)
pearls: Contraindicated in familial short QT syndrome (§4)
DRESS, incl. one death, with weekly or faster titration; none in 1339 patients started at 12.5 mg and titrated every 2 weeks (§5.1)
Taper over ≥2 weeks unless safety requires abrupt stop (§2.5)
Half-life 50–60 h (§12.3)
sources: Xcopri (cenobamate) tablets US prescribing information. SK Life Science; revised 8/2025 (user-supplied label)

Vossler DG, Gidal BE; American Epilepsy Society Treatments Committee. A Summary of Antiseizure Medications Available in the United States, 4th edition. American Epilepsy Society; revised April 1, 2024 (user-supplied)

entries.title: Perampanel (Fycompa) — maintenance dosing and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Start 2 mg once daily at bedtime; ↑ by 2 mg/day no more often than weekly. Maintenance 8–12 mg once daily (focal; some respond to 4 mg); 8 mg once daily for PGTC, up to 12 mg if tolerated
notes: 12 mg: somewhat greater seizure reduction than 8 mg, with substantially more adverse reactions (§2.1)

maintenance.agent: Perampanel — WITH moderate/strong CYP3A4 inducer (phenytoin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine)
maintenance.doseText: Start 4 mg once daily at bedtime; ↑ by 2 mg/day no more often than weekly. No established maintenance dose; highest studied 12 mg once daily

renalNotes: Mild: no adjustment; moderate: use with close monitoring, consider slower titration; severe: not recommended (§2.5, §8.7)
hepatic: Mild or moderate: start 2 mg; ↑ by 2 mg no more often than every 2 weeks; max 6 mg (mild) or 4 mg (moderate) (§2.4)
Severe: not recommended (§2.4)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation (§3)
enteral: Oral suspension 0.5 mg/mL; comparable bioavailability to tablets — interchangeable (§3, §12.3)
Suspension: shake well; use the supplied adapter and syringe; discard 90 days after opening (§2.7)
Crushing tablets or tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: No established range — AES 2024 summary Table 1
interactions: Moderate/strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, oxcarbazepine) ↓ perampanel ~50–67%; monitor and adjust when started or stopped (§7.2)
Alcohol and CNS depressants: additive CNS depression (§7.3)
pearls: Boxed warning: aggression, hostility, homicidal ideation — reduce dose if they occur; stop if severe or worsening (§5.1)
Half-life ~105 h: steady state 2–3 weeks; levels fall gradually even after abrupt stop (§5.6, §12.3)
Elderly: ↑ dose no more often than every 2 weeks (§2.6)
Falls: monitor (§5.4)
sources: Fycompa (perampanel) tablets and oral suspension US prescribing information. Catalyst Pharmaceuticals; revised 1/2024 (user-supplied label)

Vossler DG, Gidal BE; American Epilepsy Society Treatments Committee. A Summary of Antiseizure Medications Available in the United States, 4th edition. American Epilepsy Society; revised April 1, 2024 (user-supplied)

entries.title: Phenobarbital — maintenance dosing and levels (AES summary)

maintenance.doseText: Adults and children ≥13 y: initial 60 mg/day or 1–4 mg/kg/day; maintenance 1–4 mg/kg/day; adult maximum 240 mg daily
notes: Per-kg doses kept as text: the source doesn't state which weight to use
Source dose is not route-specific
No current FDA-approved adult label; AES took phenobarbital data from an older PI (1997 PDR)

renalNotes: 25–50% excreted unchanged by the kidneys; no renal dose rule in source
Elimination ↑ by diuretics, alkaline urine and activated charcoal
hepatic: Do not use in hepatic encephalopathy or marked hepatic impairment
ivPo: Forms: tablets, elixir 4 mg/mL, IV solution; oral bioavailability ~95%; source gives no IV ↔ PO conversion
enteral: Elixir 4 mg/mL
Tube administration not addressed in source — confirm with pharmacy
levels: 15–45 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
Half-life 79 h
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducer: ↑ metabolism of phenytoin, lamotrigine, oral contraceptives, warfarin, corticosteroids and many other drugs (AES Table 1)
Valproate ↓ phenobarbital elimination; MAOIs prolong its effects (AES Table 1)
Synergistic CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol and sedatives; caution with pain medications and CNS depressants (AES Table 1)
Cenobamate ↑ phenobarbital — consider reducing phenobarbital (Xcopri Table 5)
Phenobarbital ↓ oxcarbazepine MHD 25–49% (Trileptal §7.2), ↓ carbamazepine (Tegretol Precautions), shortens zonisamide half-life (Zonegran Clinical Pharmacology)
pearls: Taper very slowly after chronic use — barbiturate withdrawal can cause convulsions and delirium and may be fatal (AES Table 1)
Do not use in porphyria or marked respiratory disease (AES Table 1)
Can cause respiratory depression, hypoventilation, bradycardia and hypotension (AES Table 1)
Monitor CBC and CMP (AES Table 1)
